desc: Derive and verify the combinatorial formula $\binom{n-1}{k} \times m \times (m-1)^{n-1-k}$ based on block partitioning.
Implement a helper function for modular combination $\binom{N}{K} \pmod P$ using iterative multiplication and Fermat's Little Theorem for the modular inverse.
Implement modular exponentiation (or utilize Python's built-in `pow`) to compute $(m-1)^{n-1-k} \pmod P$ efficiently.
Combine the combinatorial and assignment components in the main method, ensuring all intermediate products are reduced modulo $10^9+7$.
Validate the implementation against edge cases ($n=1$, $m=1$, $k=0$, $k=n-1$) and provided examples.
